stories.headline: Trump Criticizes Fox News for Airing Republican Opponents Before Midterms
stories.hook: Just hours after his own Fox Business interview, President Trump took aim at the network for spotlighting Democratic challengers instead of Republican stalwarts.
stories.summary: Trump posted that Fox News devotes too much airtime to opponents of Republican candidates, whom he called American patriots with strong policies, claiming this blurs them out and keeps midterm races close. The complaint followed his appearance on Sunday Morning Futures with Larry Kudlow, amid reports of the network hosting figures like Michigan's Abdul El-Sayed. Supporters praised the direct callout on media bias, while critics dismissed it as whiny, underscoring tensions as Election Day nears.

stories.headline: Voters Overwhelmed by Endless Political Texts and Calls This Midterm Season
stories.hook: One voter hit send on a simple donation years ago and now fields texts from candidates across the country every day. The barrage has left many swearing off campaigns for good.
stories.summary: Americans are getting slammed with an average of 13 political texts and calls each week, far more than in past elections, according to a national survey. Even non-donors report daily messages from distant races, often sourced from voter records and data brokers that campaigns buy. Replying 'stop' doesn't always work, and the flood of fundraising pleas and attack ads has some installing spam blockers or vowing never to contribute again.

stories.headline: Conservatives Criticize Thune's Low-Key Midterm Push
stories.hook: With midterms 10 days away, Trump and Vance hit the trail hard while Senate Leader John Thune faces fire for staying low-profile amid stalled voting bills.
stories.summary: Conservative voices express frustration over Thune's limited visible campaigning and failure to advance the SAVE America Act, which requires photo ID for voting and citizenship proof to register. Critics call him 'basically MIA' as over 500 House bills sit idle in the Senate, even pointing to his attendance at a college football game. Thune counters that he's supported candidates in states like Iowa and stresses voter turnout, but discontent grows with pressure mounting if Republicans hold the Senate after November 3.

stories.headline: Pastor Sparks Debate on Christianity and Democratic Voting
stories.hook: Pastor Kevin Riggs shared a simple truth from his life: 'I am a Christian. I voted Democrat.' His words opened a flood of responses questioning faith and politics.
stories.summary: Riggs's post amid the 2026 midterms drew critics who argued Democratic stances on abortion, family, and sexuality clash with biblical teachings, with one comparing it to a vegetarian eating meat. Supporters countered by citing Bible verses on feeding the hungry, caring for the sick, welcoming strangers, and loving neighbors from Matthew, Luke, and Mark. The discussion highlights deep divides among Christians, as polls show white evangelicals favoring Republicans while others vary, and analyses note no biblical mandate ties faith to one party.

stories.headline: Jonah Goldberg Blames White Americans' Traits for Political Dysfunction
stories.hook: In a podcast clip, Jonah Goldberg pointed to 'neuroses' among left-wing White women and 'self-esteem issues' among right-wing White men as key drivers of U.S. political woes.
stories.summary: The Dispatch editor described these groups' personal traits as fueling dysfunction, while praising immigrants and groups like Hispanics and Indians as among the 'most patriotic and best Americans' and top Republicans. Online responses split sharply, with many criticizing the race-and-gender framing as divisive identity politics and highlighting what they see as double standards given Goldberg's Jewish background. Others urged shifting focus from demographics to everyday concerns like the economy and safety, reflecting Goldberg's own past warnings against tribal politics.

stories.headline: Gas Prices Surge Sparks Blame Game Over U.S.-Iran Conflict
stories.hook: With pumps hitting over $4 a gallon amid the U.S.-Iran war, people are pointing fingers—from Democratic energy policies to the strikes on Tehran.
stories.summary: The conflict kicked off on February 28, 2026, when U.S. and Israeli strikes targeted Iranian nuclear sites after talks failed, driving national gas averages from $2.90 to over $4 in many spots due to supply issues in the Strait of Hormuz. Conservative posts blame past Democratic moves like closing refineries and canceling the Keystone XL pipeline for weak refining capacity, while others pin the spikes squarely on the war itself. As midterms near, the back-and-forth highlights tensions between preventing a nuclear Iran, boosting domestic production, and easing household costs.

stories.headline: Prediction Markets Give Democrats 66% Chance of House and Senate Sweep Before Midterms
stories.hook: With Election Day one week away, betting markets show Democrats on track for a rare double victory in Congress. Yet reminders of past polling misses keep everyone urging voters to show up.
stories.summary: Major platforms like Polymarket list Democrats at 91% odds to take the House and 67% for the Senate, with a full sweep at 66%. Polls point to a potential 250 House seats for Democrats, their largest majority since 2008, but internal data shows Republicans closing gaps in Midwest races. Skeptics cite contradictions like a CNN Senate map favoring Republicans 53-46 and the 2016 New York Times forecast that gave Hillary Clinton a 92% edge she didn't win. Both sides push turnout, questioning if markets and polls will match reality.

stories.headline: Online Hopes for Right-Wing Losses in Brazil, Israel, and US Elections
stories.hook: One post imagined a single week sweeping out Bolsonaro in Brazil, Netanyahu in Israel, and Republican majorities in the US Congress. It quickly drew tens of thousands of likes from those rooting for the shift.
stories.summary: A message on October 24 envisioned defeats for right-wing figures in upcoming votes: Brazil's presidential runoff on Sunday pitting Senator Flávio Bolsonaro against President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, Israel's Knesset elections on Tuesday where Netanyahu's coalition trails or ties the opposition, and US midterms on November 3 with narrow Republican majorities at risk in the House and Senate. Polls show all three races neck-and-neck, fueling both optimism and skepticism online. Some called the scenario unlikely or dismissed opposition candidates as similar problems, highlighting the tight uncertainties ahead.
